title: Neural Stored-program Memory with Mirror programs
hypothesis: A small task program coordinate over a shared recurrent controller basis can match held-out program interpolation quality with fewer bytes than an NSPM-style key-value memory of full anchor programs.
mirror_coordinate: per-task two-dimensional program code m=(z1,z2) over A0/B1/B2
logical_multiplicity: 23 aligned task controllers from shared state plus one unrelated private controller

selection.method: secrets.randbelow over sorted eligible P0/UNTESTED IDs after exclusions

task.task_coordinate_provenance: held-out z values are supplied context; the 23 stored task addresses are serialized in each method payload

teacher.private_program: independent full controller matrix for task index 23
teacher.program_source: A0/B1/B2 and one private matrix are synthetic teacher objects; no gradient training or learned memory keys

development.purpose: validate serializer and interpolation metric only; no fresh tuning

success_gate: All three fresh worlds have normalized held-out trajectory MSE <=1e-5; Mirror payload <=0.90x NSPM corner memory; Mirror controller/interpolation MACs <=1.25x NSPM; report comparison against ordinary shared-basis control.
mirror_specific_gate: Mirror payload <=0.90x ordinary shared matrix-basis control at matched quality.
failure_gate: Fresh quality or NSPM storage/compute gate fails, or ordinary shared-basis control matches Mirror within 10% bytes at matched quality.
boundaries: Synthetic recurrent linear controller family only; not a full NSPM reproduction.
Task coordinates are supplied context and charged equally to memory and Mirror methods.
One unrelated task is stored privately.
No neural query/router learning, non-affine task family, or language model is tested.
